## Objectives

General information about the project.

Project goals:

-  Binary sentimental classification between hate and non hate speech. 

Data Sources:

- Automated Hate Speech Detection and the Problem of Offensive Language [@mrmorj2022kaggle]
- DistilBert pretrained model [@sanh2019distilbert]
- Test evaluation data [@ashwiniyer176_toxic_tweets]

## Methodology
Implementation of a learning algorithm for binary classification capable of distinguishing clear and cloudy skies.

- Text Preprocessing: Removes;
  - Removes Emails
  - Removes IP addresses
  - Removes Punctuation
  - Removes Numbers
  - Removes stopwords using NLTK
  - Tokenizes words.

#![Data preprocessing]("C:\Users\Sijibomi\Documents\LTU\AIKMR\Datapreprocessing.png")

 
## 1. Model Training and Logging

- Custom Bidirectional LSTM model using Amazon hate speech data:

  - Uses Tokenizer and pad_sequences.

  - Train/val/test split.

  - Simple architecture: Embedding → BiLSTM → Dense.

  - Uses binary_crossentropy, tracks accuracy.
  
- Logs:

  - Loss/accuracy (train & val) to TensorBoard.

  - Confusion matrix

  - Word & sentence embeddings

  - Text predictions with probabilities
 
## 2. Pretrained DistilBERT model (if use_pretrained=True)

- Loads Amazon Polarity dataset (subset).

- Tokenized using DistilBertTokenizerFast.

- Sets class weights to handle imbalance.

- Uses Hugging Face's Trainer with a custom WeightedLossTrainer.

- Logs:

  - Train/test accuracy to TensorBoard

  - Test set embeddings (from CLS token)
  
## 3. Evaluation on Unlabeled Data: evaluate_on_unlabeled_data(...)

- Preprocesses and tokenizes new input data.

- Runs model inference on either:

- Keras model: generates predictions, sentence embeddings

- Pretrained model: uses BERT’s CLS token output as embeddings

- Logs to TensorBoard:

  - Predictions and probabilities

  - Text with predicted vs. true labels

  - Confusion matrix (if labels available)

  - Sentence embeddings
